subject: Re: Post-demo: model regression after v2.1.0 update (Acme POC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — model regression after v2.1.0 update

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and immediate next steps from our side after reviewing the benchmarks you shared:

Summary:
- During your POC run you observed a quality drop after the model runtime update (v2.1.0). The increase in hallucinations and longer-form factual errors was most noticeable on your customer-support prompt set.
- We ran a controlled benchmark comparing the model pinned to v2.0.3 vs the runtime-picked v2.1.0 and reproduced a statistically significant regression on the same evaluation prompts (see attached acme_benchmark_report_v2.0.3_vs_v2.1.0.pdf).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I recommend we pin your POC to model runtime v2.0.3 while our infra team investigates. This will preserve current quality while we root-cause.
2) Rishi and team will prepare a short diff summary (quantization/kernel/runtime changes) and a rollback plan.
3) Please share any additional failing examples (sample_bad_responses.txt is helpful) and confirm if we should proceed with a canary rollback on your staging environment tomorrow morning.

Attachments: acme_benchmark_report_v2.0.3_vs_v2.1.0.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.csv

Recommended model/config: redwood-llama-70b-q4f16 pinned to runtime v2.0.3 for now; we can test v2.1.0 again after fixes.

I'll c+c Rishi and Sean to coordinate the rollback plan. Let me know approval to proceed.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — model regression after v2.1.0 update

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for reproducing our findings. We do want to keep the POC moving but the hallucination rate jumped from ~2.1% to ~6.7% on our customer-support test set after the update — that's high enough to block the next phase.

I've attached the logs and a small set of failing examples (acme_sample_bad_responses.txt) from our staging runs. If pinning to v2.0.3 is low-risk, please go ahead — we need the baseline behavior back.

Also: can you confirm whether any prompt-engineering changes might explain the delta? We didn't change prompt templates between runs.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lin
Head of AI Product, Acme Corp
sara.lin@acme.com

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — model regression after v2.1.0 update

Thanks for the reports and the sample failures, Sara — I dug into the runtime traces and ran a diff between v2.0.3 and v2.1.0 on your prompt set. High-level summary attached (diff_summary_v2.0.3_vs_v2.1.0.txt).

Preliminary findings:
- v2.1.0 introduced an updated kernel selection that enables an alternative attention kernel on certain sequence-lengths and a more aggressive quantization fallback for long-context batches.
- The regression correlates with a subset of prompts where the model falls back to the alternative kernel + the new quant path; those cases show increased token-level entropy (more unexpected tokens).
- No changes detected to the public prompt templates or your prompt pre-processing pipeline.

Suggested immediate actions:
1) Pin the POC to runtime v2.0.3 (no model change) — low risk, quick to apply.
2) We'll run a targeted canary of v2.1.0 with stricter quantization thresholds and longer prefix caching enabled to see whether the kernel selection or quantization is the driver.
3) If the canary fails, we will roll forward a mitigation in the runtime that forces kernel selection parity with v2.0.3 for your account.

Rollback plan (high level):
- Apply runtime pin at the account layer for Acme (config change) — expected downtime: none; immediate effect for new sessions.
- Launch canary on a small subset of your staging traffic (controlled percentage) with conservative runtime flags.
- If canary passes, re-evaluate enabling v2.1.0 with the mitigation flags; if not, extend the pin until full fix is available.

I attached the diff summary and will follow up with a short runbook for the account pin + rollback steps. Do we have approval to apply the pin asap?

- Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
